titleEn: At the Back of the Line, Take Your Turn!

pages.text: "The first bread smells wonderful!" Coco, a little mouse in a red headscarf, hurried down from the loft. Outside the shop, the line of customers stretched into the alley. "I want the first bite of the hot first bread!"

"Me first!" Coco scurried beside the line and squeezed in at the front. Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, was pushed back, with one foot lifting off the stones. Coco didn't look behind.
The customers behind him jostled and wobbled. Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, stopped with her bread paddle in hand. "Coco, what about the customers behind you?"
Grandpa crouched in front of Coco. "How would you feel if I squeezed in ahead of you?" Coco thought hard. "...I'd feel upset."
Grandpa smiled gently. "Join a line at the back. Take turns, and everyone gets some." Coco's mouth turned up. "At the back of the line, take your turn!"
Coco walked to the very back, at the end of the alley. Rows of customers' backs stood ahead; the shop door was far away. Coco shuffled their feet but kept waiting.
The line moved forward a little at a time. Grandpa came out with crescent bread and waved a paw at Coco. Coco waved too and sang softly, "At the back of the line, take your turn!"
At last, Coco's turn! Mom handed over steaming crescent bread. Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws. "After waiting, it feels even hotter!" A big bite. Yum, yum!

The next morning, Coco ran straight to the back of the line at the alley's end. "One, join at the back! Two, wait for my turn! Three, once I have mine, the next customer!" Another customer stood behind Coco.

Mom set down the bread paddle and hugged Coco warmly. "Bread you waited for tastes best, doesn't it?" Join at the back, and both you and I get some. Coco held the bread and called, "At the back of the line, take your turn!"
